conventions.commits: Conventional Commits with types (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore); all commits must be GPG-signed and signed-off with DCO (git commit -S --signoff)
conventions.testing: Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs and semantic_correctness.rs; test patterns include parse_and_extract, inheritance extraction, and call site detection
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo deny check advisories licenses; workspace lints deny undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (with test exemptions)
conventions.error_handling: Use Result<T, E> with thiserror; no unwrap/expect in production code; bounds checking with .get() instead of indexing on untrusted data

patterns: Language modules follow pattern: const ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, then optional handler functions (extract_function_name, extract_inheritance, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver)

LanguageInfo struct fields: name, language (tree-sitter Language), element_query, call_query, reference_query (Option), import_query (Option), impl_query (Option), impl_trait_query (Option), defuse_query (Option), extract_function_name (Option handler), find_method_for_receiver (Option handler), find_receiver_type (Option handler), extract_inheritance (Option handler)
Registration occurs in three places: (1) EXTENSION_MAP in lang.rs, (2) mod.rs pub mod declarations, (3) get_language_info() match arm, (4) get_ts_language() match arm, (5) supported_languages() slice
Tree-sitter queries use capture groups with @-suffixes to tag declaration kinds (e.g., @function, @class, @interface) and field names (e.g., @method_name, @class_name)
DEFUSE_QUERY pattern: capture local variable declarations with @write.local, assignments with @write.assign, updates with @writeread.update, and all identifier reads with @read.usage
Inheritance extraction walks parent nodes or inspects base_clause/class_interface_clause fields to find extends/implements names

related_issues.title: Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php
related_issues.relevance: This is the issue being researched

constraints: PHP grammar uses base_clause and class_interface_clause as child nodes, not fields on class_declaration (unlike Java's superclass/interfaces fields)
PHP function_definition is the top-level function node; method_declaration is nested inside class/interface/trait bodies
PHP has trait_declaration and interface_declaration as distinct node types alongside class_declaration
PHP enums (enum_declaration) are a distinct type with enum_declaration_list body and optional class_interface_clause for implements
Tree-sitter-php grammar uses 'name' field (not 'identifier' child) for function, class, interface, trait, enum names
test_coverage: Existing tests cover function/class/interface/enum extraction (test_java_parse_and_extract), inheritance extraction (semantic_correctness tests), import detection, and call site detection. No PHP-specific tests exist yet; new integration tests must cover: function_definition extraction, method_declaration extraction, class_declaration with extends/implements, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, and DEFUSE_QUERY for local variable tracking.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; grammar defines function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration node types with 'name' field; base_clause and class_interface_clause as optional children for inheritance
library_findings.notes: Tree-sitter-php is actively maintained and covers modern PHP (8.0+) including enums, union types, attributes, and property hooks. Grammar source at https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php; node-types.json at php/src/node-types.json and php_only/src/node-types.json

library_findings.relevant_api: Language, Query, QueryCursor, Node types and field access via child_by_field_name(); tree-sitter query syntax for pattern matching
library_findings.notes: Core parsing library used by all language handlers; queries are compiled once and reused for performance

approaches.name: Approach 1: Minimal PHP support (functions, classes, interfaces only)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition, class_declaration, interface_declaration; CALL_QUERY for method calls; no DEFUSE_QUERY or inheritance extraction. Register in mod.rs, lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP (.php), get_language_info(), get_ts_language(). Add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml workspace dependencies. Write 5-6 integration tests.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Full PHP support with inheritance but no DEFUSE_QUERY
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration. Implement extract_inheritance() handler to walk base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes. Add CALL_QUERY for method invocations. Register in all 4 places (mod.rs, lang.rs, get_language_info, get_ts_language). Add tree-sitter-php dependency. Write 8-10 integration tests covering all declaration kinds and inheritance.

approaches.name: Approach 3: Complete PHP support with DEFUSE_QUERY (recommended)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with full ELEMENT_QUERY (all 6 declaration kinds), CALL_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY (local variable declarations, assignments, identifier reads), and extract_inheritance() handler. DEFUSE_QUERY is required because PHP has complex variable scoping (superglobals, dynamic variables, closures with use() clauses) and tracking local vs. global is essential for accurate analysis. Register in all 4 places. Add tree-sitter-php. Write 12+ integration tests covering declarations, inheritance, method calls, and variable definition/use sites.
pros: Enables variable tracking and data-flow analysis
Supports future control-flow and taint-tracking features
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for accurate scope analysis in PHP
cons: Requires careful DEFUSE_QUERY design to handle PHP-specific patterns (superglobals, dynamic variables)

recommendation: Approach 3 (Complete PHP support with DEFUSE_QUERY). Justification: (1) DEFUSE_QUERY is required because PHP's variable scoping is complex (superglobals like $_GET, $_POST, dynamic variables via $$var, and closures with use() clauses) — accurate analysis must distinguish local declarations from global references. (2) The codebase already has DEFUSE_QUERY patterns in Java, Python, and Rust; PHP should follow the same pattern for consistency. (3) The tree-sitter-php grammar is mature and well-documented; all node types and fields are stable. (4) Integration tests can be written incrementally. (5) This approach enables future features like taint tracking and control-flow analysis.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
(
  (function_definition
    name: (name) @function_name) @function
  (method_declaration
    name: (name) @method_name) @function
  (class_declaration
    name: (name) @class_name) @class
  (interface_declaration
    name: (name) @interface_name) @class
  (trait_declaration
    name: (name) @trait_name) @class
  (enum_declaration
    name: (name) @enum_name) @class
)
inheritance_walk_citation: For a class_declaration node in tree-sitter-php grammar, inheritance is captured via optional child nodes (not fields): (1) Walk the class_declaration's children to find base_clause node — if present, extract its named_type child to get the extends class name. (2) Walk the class_declaration's children to find class_interface_clause node — if present, iterate its named_type children to get each implements interface name. Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js shows class_declaration rule uses optional($.base_clause) and optional($.class_interface_clause); https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/php/src/node-types.json confirms class_declaration fields are only: attributes, body, name (no parent_class or interfaces fields).
